title: Reliability ops alignment checklist — Q2 2026
content:
Objective:
Deliver a pragmatic, cross-team operational checklist and short roadmap to incubate, validate, and graduate Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for customer-facing inference APIs and internal control-plane endpoints. Focus: measurable SLOs (latency and availability), dashboard coverage, oncall playbooks, and a repeatable handoff to product and infra teams.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Candidate services: api-gateway, generation-service, model-routing, cache-layer, private-control-plane
- SLO types: latency p50/p95 for core routes, availability (synthetic success rate), and queueing/backpressure indicators
- Cross-functional owners: SRE (lead), Serving Runtime, Platform, Observability, Product-hosted-api
- Excludes: model quality/regression metrics (handled by Optimize team), billing/quota SLOs (billing infra)

Deliverables (minimal viable set for incubation):
1) Proposed SLO spec per service (objective, target, measurement window, error budget policy)
2) Prometheus/Datadog queries and a Prom-to-DD translation mapping for each SLO
3) Dashboard template (critical widgets + runbook links)
4) One playbook per SLO for oncall automation and mitigation steps
5) Post-mortem template and escalation flow for SLO burn

Milestones & timeline (Q2 2026):
- Week 1 (Mar 10–16): Stakeholder kickoff, finalize candidate services, collect current metrics and SLIs (who has what)
- Week 2 (Mar 17–23): Draft SLO specs; infra owners sign off on metric availability
- Week 3–4 (Mar 24–Apr 6): Implement metrics gaps (exporters, synthetic probes), create dashboards (obs team + serving runtime)
- Week 5 (Apr 7–13): Small-scale pilot on api-gateway + generation-service; validate measurement fidelity
- Week 6–8 (Apr 14–May 4): Iterate thresholds, create runbooks, automate alerting and burn tracking
- Week 9–12 (May 5–Jun 1): Gradual rollout to remaining services, final review, handoff to product owners for production SLO contract

Owners & responsibilities (primary contacts):
- SRE (Priya Menon) — overall coordination, SLO policy, alerts and burn tracking
- Observability (Aisha Patel) — dashboards, queries, synthetic probe implementation, instrumentation reviews
- Serving Runtime (Miguel Torres) — surface relevant SLIs (latency by route, cache hit rate), assist on kernel-level metrics
- Platform Engineering (Claire Nguyen) — telemetry export, Prometheus scrape configs, infra quotas for synthetic probes
- Product-hosted-api (Ben Turner) — validate business-level targets, accept SLO contract for public APIs

Measurement details (examples / to copy):
- Latency SLI: request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"} => p50/p95 computed over 5m sliding window; SLO: p95 < 350ms (rolling 30d, 90% window)
- Availability SLI: synthetic_success_rate{probe="api-gateway"} => success = 2xx + 4xx allowed? (decide) ; SLO: 99.9%/30d
- Error SLI: server_error_ratio = sum(status=5xx)/sum(total) over 1h -> alert if > 1% for 15m
Notes: We need to standardize what counts as a user-visible failure (4xx vs 5xx decision open).

Dashboards & alerts (minimum):
- Service-level dashboard: current burn, p50/p95, traffic, error budget remaining, synthetic probe HDD plot
- Incident view: top endpoints by errors, recent deploys, recent config changes (link to deploy metadata)
- Burn pager: Slack channel + automated JIRA ticket when burn > 20% in 7d

Runbooks (example bullets):
- If p95 spikes > 2x baseline: check recent deploys -> roll back if correlated; check cache-layer latency and eviction rate; scale serving pool if CPU-backed queueing visible
- If synthetic probe fails regionally: validate routing (CDN, edge), check region capacity, fallback to other region routing policy

Risks & open questions (short list):
- Metric fidelity: some kernels expose only end-to-end timing, not per-queue breakdown. Need minimal exporter changes.
- Definition drift: product owners may want different SLO windows; propose core defaults but allow per-API overrides with approval process.
- Alert noise: naive burn alerts create churn. We must tune to burn velocity not instantaneous spikes.

Next actions (next two weeks):
- [Priya] Run stakeholder kickoff (Mar 12) — invite listed owners + billing lead
- [Aisha] Inventory existing dashboards and post links (Mar 15) — add to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-12345
- [Miguel] List metrics missing from serving-runtime and estimate implementation cost (Mar 19)
- [Claire] Add synthetic probe capacity estimate and tentative scrape changes (Mar 20)
- [Ben] Confirm business targets for /v1/generate & private control-plane endpoints (Mar 22)

Decision log (working):
- Temporary decision: treat 4xx as user errors for availability SLI unless rate of 4xx increases > 3x baseline (revisit after pilot)

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Pilot on api-gateway first: low blast radius, high visibility. If probe detects SLO burn, can route traffic to dedicated cache/edge variant as fallback.
- Consider adding per-model routing SLOs later (dependent on model-specific tail latency).
- Keep this doc as the canonical checklist during incubation; transfer final SLO contracts to product Confluence page (link above) once signed off.

References & links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-12345 (SRE SLO incubation master)
- Jira epic: JIRA-SRE-3421
- Telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/88

Status: draft. Comments welcome — add inline or ping Priya in #sre-team.

-- end of checklist (working copy)
